A month, or a year, as one ring

The fourth icon in the dial switcher draws a whole month — or a whole year — as a single circle. One ray per day, its length the share of your active window that is committed, its colour whichever event colour covered most of that day. The year is divided by its real days, so February is narrower than March and a leap year is one ray wider.

DAYLIGHT
The hours between sunset and sunrise are softly shaded right on the 24-hour ring, with a thin mark at each horizon. Its own switch, off by default, 24-hour dial only. When the forecast gave no sunrise or sunset, nothing is drawn: a day we were not told about is not the same as a day without a night.

ROUTINES, ONE STEP AT A TIME
A checklist can be walked one item at a time, each with its own timer and its own voice. And when starting is the hard part, "Break into steps" proposes three to seven steps with a length each. A proposal, not an order: you choose how many, and they are added to the list you already have rather than replacing it.

YOUR PHONE'S CALENDARS
The device's own calendars can be drawn faintly on the dial. They are read on the device and never uploaded — the server does not see them. Offered before you even sign up, so the first dial is not empty.

A ROUTINE AS A WEB PAGE
A saved routine opens as a link in any browser, with its steps, its lengths and its ring. If you want, it can be submitted to the public directory; until then only someone with the link can read it, and search engines are told to skip it. Withdrawing from the directory is instant and needs nobody's permission.

A DAY, A MONTH OR A YEAR AS ONE PICTURE
The ring saves as an image, with three numbers under it: hours, events, and the percentage of your active window. Event titles never leave the device this way.

MEDS × ENERGY
A long press on the pill badge shows how many heavy minutes today, and how many of them fall inside the effect window you described yourself. An observation, never a prescription: it moves nothing and scores no day.

CYCLE AND ENERGY BUDGET
The cycle week can be shaded on the calendar, and what it costs is yours to decide, not the app's.

CALMER NOTIFICATIONS
Low-pressure mode now reaches notifications too: an offer instead of a task, with no "should" and no "must". The same trip gave every notification four languages instead of two. The mode changes HOW something is said and never whether it is sent — that is still quiet hours and your notification settings.

PIN
The local PIN now covers the cycle screen as well, not only the emotion diary.

SMALLER THINGS

DAY REWIND
• A few hours before your usual bedtime, your day is ready. Open it and your mascot walks it from last night to right now, over hills of calm and stress.

WEATHER ON YOUR WRIST

Forge 1.3.4 opens your files where they are, gives every statement its own result, and puts the results grid on the keyboard.

FILES OPENED IN PLACE
A DuckDB, SQLite, CSV, JSON, or SQL dump file you choose is no longer copied into Forge: it opens in place, and a file you move or rename is found again. When a dlt pipeline or a script writes to the same DuckDB or SQLite file, Refresh shows the new data; CSV, JSON, and SQL dump files are read when the connection opens. To write to a SQLite or DuckDB file outside Forge's own folder, allow access to its folder once (the button explains why). Connections created earlier keep their copy until you choose the file again.

QUERY EDITOR
Several statements separated by semicolons give one result per statement, with a selector above the grid. psql-style parameters :name, :'name', and :"name" work alongside {{name}} (on Oracle, :name stays a server bind variable). The autocomplete popup on Mac no longer replaces the schema you typed before the dot, and a semicolon typed while the popup is open leaves your text intact. Outside ClickHouse, a table or column named settings or format no longer breaks the default LIMIT.

RESULTS GRID
The selected row keeps keyboard focus: Up/Down, Home/End, and Page Up/Down move the selection, Left/Right pick a cell, Return edits that cell in an editable table, and Escape cancels. Command-C copies the selected row as tab-separated text, or the picked cell. The inspector has a Values pane showing every column of the selected row, in the data browser and in query results. On iPhone, Row Details in the long-press menu shows the same list.

If you use Yuni to track your own cycle, it sometimes wrote about you as though you were someone else's partner — "Remember what she mentioned last week", on your own screen. We went through every place Yuni writes text and fixed it: notifications, Live Activities, the calendar, the intimacy log, settings and your insights.

The same pass found that hormonal contraception was only half handled. Yuni would hide your phase and then predict one anyway — "PMS in 3 days" — with phase-based advice still sitting underneath. On contraception it no longer claims a phase it cannot know, and the advice changes with the setting instead of staying behind.

On Home, the line about your next phase was showing a piece of raw code where the number of days should be. It says what it meant to say now, in every language.

Check-in and the intimacy log moved to the bottom left of Home and are now the same, larger size — easier to reach with one thumb, and no longer covering the period button.

On Reports, the button that creates one used to sit below everything else, off the bottom of smaller screens. It now stays above the tab bar, in view.

Fifteen screens in tracking mode were still in English for some of you. They are translated now.

Purchases are now linked to your Yuni account rather than to the device they were made on.

In contraception mode the daily suggestion is no longer picked at random. Yuni reads your last few check-ins and leads with what they point at — rest and sleep after a low-energy week, time to yourself after you have been asking for space — and says which it is, in the line underneath. Until you have logged enough for that to mean anything, it says nothing rather than guessing.

That came with a quieter fix. What you told Yuni helps you, and what you asked it to avoid, were only ever being applied in English. On this screen they now work in every language.

Apple Pay purchases arrive already filed

The category is there the moment the purchase lands

The ones it could not place wait in one line
A purchase that arrived without a category shows up in the review banner on the transactions list. Tap its notification and the categorize sheet opens on that purchase to pick one. You will know if the receipt cannot reach you
That notification is the receipt for a purchase logged while the app was closed. With notifications switched off the purchase would be saved in silence, so the Apple Pay screen now says so and takes you to the setting.

Big ledgers open instantly

Continuum runs on one number now. Your consistency — the share of the last 66 days you showed up — sits on every card as a small readout. The triangle beside it is this week's move. The home screen pools every habit into one figure.

I built this app around streaks for a year, freezes included. That was the wrong number. A streak turns one bad day into zero; consistency turns it into a dip. Freezes are gone. So is the 8pm "streak ends at midnight" alert, replaced by a single nudge on the evening after a miss. Never miss twice.

Color follows the grid. A habit starts coral red and turns blue as its 66 days fill — a week-old habit at 100% is still coral, because blue takes time as well as showing up.

A habit is formed after 66 days with at least 80% of them done. Sixty-six is the median it took people in a UCL study for a daily habit to become automatic, and one missed day didn't materially slow it down. The 80% is my line; the study doesn't set one. Already there? It's formed the next time you mark it done.

New habits don't start near zero any more: the number counts from your first day, so 20 days out of 20 reads 100% (it used to read 30%).

The stats screen shows your last 12 weeks as bars. Watch them climb.

Bug Fixes and Performance Improvements

Updated Visual Design
We've made subtle but impactful updates to the app's overall design. Mood Tracker now features a cleaner layout, improved spacing, and a refreshed interface to help you focus on what matters most—your emotional wellbeing. The mood logging screen has been streamlined for quicker, easier entries, and the dashboard is now easier to read and navigate.

New Mood Icons and Images
To better reflect the full range of human emotions, we’ve updated and added new mood icons. These changes are designed to help you more accurately capture how you feel each day. Alongside this, we've refreshed some of the in-app visuals to make journaling a more enjoyable and intuitive experience.

User Experience Enhancements
You’ll notice improved flow throughout the app. From opening the app to completing your daily entry, everything has been optimized for ease and clarity. Navigating between past entries, dashboards, and journaling prompts is now more intuitive.

Improved Daily Reminders
We've adjusted the reminder system to be more flexible and helpful. You now have more control over when and how you're prompted to check in each day. Whether you prefer morning reflections or evening reviews, reminders are now easier to customize to your routine.

Privacy and Offline Access
As always, your data remains private and secure. Mood Tracker continues to function entirely offline, with no account or internet connection required. Your journal is your personal space, and this update reinforces our commitment to privacy and user control.

Finalist 4.1 is ready for the latest iOS, here are the highlights.

SIRI AND APPLE INTELLIGENCE (iOS 27)
Siri can now manage Finalist directly. Create, update, complete and delete tasks, take notes, and manage calendar events, all conversationally. Say "Add a task in Finalist", or say the whole thing in one sentence and it goes right in. Use Finalist regularly and Siri learns it is your planner, so you can even drop the app name. Tasks and notes appear in Spotlight too, so Siri can find and open them by name.

WEEKLY SPREAD
A new Planner mode that lays out your week like a paper planner spread: Monday to Wednesday on the left page, Thursday to Sunday on the right. iPad and Mac show the open spread and flip whole weeks, iPhone turns one page at a time. A new visual layout picker lets you show or hide any kind of content (tasks, reminders, habits, events, weather) in every Planner mode.

SCORE
An opt-in Daily section that turns a week of scattered effort into one number. Give your tags point values, set a weekly target, and earn points by completing tasks, habits and reminders, or simply journaling. A new History view shows half a year of week-by-week results, with streaks and your best week. Turn it on in Customize Layout.

DAY NOTES AND SKETCHES
Daily's Notes section now has a permanent spot to jot things down. Start typing and it becomes today's note. Tap the pencil tab to sketch instead, with Apple Pencil or a finger, right inside Daily. Drawings use Apple's modern Pencil engine with shapes, text boxes and stickers, and sketches now show up on the Mac.

MULTI-SELECTION
Pick a bunch of tasks in Daily and complete, move, tag or delete them in one go, with Undo. Cmd-click on Mac and iPad, two-finger tap on iPhone. The Timeline gets multi-select too: group blocks and move them together, gaps preserved.

ALSO IN 4.1
- A new full-page Day Page widget, built for iOS 27's extra-large widget size.
- Tags: a two-page workspace with usage details, Time Spent reports, twenty new ink colors and a custom color picker.

- Text size control in Settings, reaching most of the app.

- Photos and sketches move to new synced storage with much higher quality and size limits.
- Apple Watch: reschedule reminders from the wrist, and a cleaner tap model on rows.

First, I fixed a ton of bugs and crashes on iOS 27. I went through every tool: saving and exporting, dark mode, and how things behave when your phone is low on memory or storage

There’s a new tool, Mini Vlog. You shoot short clips (1–3 sec) throughout the day, and Zebra puts them together into one video. You can add the time, place, weather, and step count to your clips, plus text with an entrance animation, photos, and stickers

I’m launching AI video. Pick a template, add a photo, and get a short video, like you riding your giant cat. While the video is being made, you can close Zebra: I’ll send a push notification when it’s ready. I’m rolling it out gradually, and it’ll be available to everyone soon

I added 7 new handwritten fonts. I also sorted the fonts into categories, added “Popular” and “New” sections, and added favourites: press and hold a font to add it to your favourites. It works in “Text on Photo,” collages, and carousels

“Text on Photo” now has blurred text, the shadow is stronger, and you can change the font with one button right above the layer

Story series are here, for when you want to tell a story across several stories in a row. Select all your photos at once, and Zebra creates a separate story for each one in the order you picked them. You can leave a note on each one about what to say in it, so you don’t forget your idea. Design the stories one by one, and when everything’s ready, save the whole series to your gallery with one tap, without opening each one separately. You can also duplicate a series along with its notes and make a new one from it

I added a bunch of new story templates

Filters are now sorted into groups, with a “New” section and favourites. Carousels got new effects: blur, darkening, bottom shadow, and grain

I built my own photo crop tool: you can drag any edge, choose proportions like wallpaper, YouTube, 3:2, or 21:9, rotate, flip, and undo a step. I rewrote the “Before/After” tool from scratch: live preview, smooth 60 frames per second, and 7 divider colours

There are now widgets with quick tools on your Home Screen and Lock Screen. You choose the tools in “Settings” → “Widgets”, and it’s handy to put the Mini Vlog tool there

And a few smaller things: blur now has undo and redo, collages let you adjust the spacing between letters and lines, the Share menu is more convenient, and videos can get darkening, blur, and grain with a live preview. “Memories” got zoom and video scrubbing, and AI styles got a “Popular” section

P.S. As always, thank you for your feedback — I read every message, and it really means a lot to me)
P.P.S. You can now reach me through the new feedback form in “Settings”: choose a topic and attach a screenshot or video if you need to. I’m always open to your ideas and suggestions ◕‿◕

Hello everyone!

Subtrack 1.10.3 is a reliability update. It fixes the issues many of you reported, makes your numbers more accurate, and adds a few small touches.

What's fixed and improved in 1.10.3:

- Fixed subscriptions going stale when you didn't open the app for a while. A paused subscription could land in the Ended tab after its pause was over, and price changes or trial endings could be missed. Everything now catches up the next time you open Subtrack, including subscriptions already affected.
- Widgets now stay accurate even when the app stays closed. Due dates keep moving forward on their own, and the Calendar widget now shows every billing date in the month, not just the next one.
- Fixed a sync issue that could remove a Space when using Subtrack on more than one device. Your subscriptions were never deleted. If a Space went missing, its subscriptions are still under All Spaces.
- On Mac, Subtrack no longer opens on its own. Launch at Login is now off unless you turn it on, and when it is on, Subtrack starts quietly in the menu bar.
- New setting on iPad and Mac: Remember Sidebar. Hide or show the sidebar, and Subtrack opens the same way next time.
- Reminders are more reliable. You now get a reminder when the first bill is still in the future, one before every charge on fixed-length plans, and the reminder shows the price for that date.
- More accurate totals. Fixed payments that could be counted twice when you recorded a different billing day, free trials missing from your average spending, the monthly amount for fixed-length plans, calendar totals that mixed currencies, and totals shifting after an offline currency update.
- Cleaner subscription cards, with better logo alignment, smoother corners, and long prices that no longer wrap.
- Fixed a crash when switching between sidebar items on iPad and Mac, and a crash when turning off Free Trial while editing a subscription.

Thank you for continuing to use Subtrack and for all the feedback. If you like the app, kindly leave a review on the App Store. Reviews really help Subtrack reach more people. You can also follow @subtrackapp on X for updates, and if you would like to support Subtrack's development even further, you can leave a tip from the Tip Jar in Settings.

Stay tuned! :)

Bug fixes

- Sorting by author. When sorting by author, some surnames landed in the wrong place: Johnson before Johns, Dawson before Daws. A surname now always comes before longer ones that start the same way, apostrophes are ignored (O'Brien after Obama), and a hyphen counts as a space. This also applies to translators, narrators, illustrators, categories, and publishers.
- Articles in the book's language. With "Ignore leading articles when sorting" on, articles from every language were ignored: an English book like "Die For Love" landed under F, because "Die" is a German article. Now only the articles of the book's language are ignored; for a book with no language set, those of every language.
- Titles with apostrophes and hyphens. When sorting by title, apostrophes are now ignored and a hyphen counts as a space: "Jo's Boys" comes after "Johann", "Hard-boiled" before "Hard Land".
- Series. When sorting by series, the name no longer loses its leading article: "The Wheel of Time" is under T.

The new order is applied automatically the first time you open the app after updating.

- Reading year recap in Statistics, written with Apple Intelligence.
- Tag and category suggestions when you assign them to a book. They are never applied on their own: you decide.
- A switch in Settings to turn the Apple Intelligence features on or off.
- Many new actions for Siri and Shortcuts, which also understand the book, quote, note, or goal on screen. Get quotes, notes, ratings, milestones, and your yearly recap as an image, a PDF, or rich text.
- Your books in Spotlight search, in system suggestions, and in the widget Smart Stack.
- Reading session Live Activity refined: timer always readable, cover shown correctly, StandBy and landscape Dynamic Island, pause and resume right from the Live Activity.
- Export a book, your library, quotes, or notes as PDF.
- Importing rebuilt from the ground up: Book Tracker recognises the file, shows you row by row what will happen, and can update the books you already have. Rows that could not be imported come back in a file that explains why.
- Library search ignores case, accents, and punctuation; title sorting is more consistent and can ignore leading articles. "Repair search and sorting" in Settings rebuilds that data if needed.

Some of these features require a device compatible with Apple Intelligence.

Well. We did it again.

We’ve moved a lot of things around.

Before you close the app forever, hear us out.

The goal wasn’t to make you relearn StrengthLog from scratch. The goal was to make it make more sense. Things now live where they always should have lived. Your profile is now home to... well, your stuff (like exercises you create, programs you build, achievements you get, etc.). Statistics has taken custody of all the statistics. Exercises have moved into the Library. And each exercise page has become the one-stop shop for everything related to that exercise.

Will your muscle memory hate us for a week? Probably.

Will future you thank us? We think so.

Here’s what else is new:

• The top of your home screen now has a calendar where you can start workouts, plan future workouts, add events, and even backlog workouts you forgot to log. (We won’t judge. Much.)

WORKOUT CREATION WITH NATURAL LANGUAGE
Create a complete, personalized workout simply by describing what you want. Tell SmartGym your goals, training frequency, preferred muscle groups, available time, or other requirements, and Smart Trainer turns your request into structured routines with exercises, sets, reps, rest times, and more.

NATURAL LANGUAGE WORKOUTS ON APPLE WATCH
Create personalized workouts with natural language directly from Apple Watch, independently of iPhone. Describe the workout you want, and SmartGym builds the complete routine right on your wrist.

SIRI AI
SmartGym deeply integrates with Siri AI, making routines, exercises, equipment, muscle groups, and other training information accessible through natural voice requests. Siri AI can surface relevant SmartGym information directly and take you to the corresponding content when needed.

RICH WORKOUT INFORMATION IN SIRI AI
View workout summaries, recent training history, muscle recovery, goals, and other SmartGym information directly in Siri AI, with rich visual results that don’t require opening the app.

ONSCREEN SIRI AWARENESS
Siri AI can understand key SmartGym content currently visible on screen. Ask about routines, exercises, or upcoming sets, then continue naturally with commands such as opening an item or logging the next set.

CREATE WORKOUTS FROM TEXT WITH SIRI AI
Dictate or create an entire workout as plain text with Siri AI and ask it to save the workout to SmartGym. SmartGym converts the unstructured text into a complete, ready-to-use routine.

IMPROVED EXERCISE QUESTIONS
Exercise Questions now uses exercise execution images alongside Apple’s on-device Foundation Models, providing better contextual answers about movements in SmartGym’s library of more than 730 exercises.  

RESIZABLE INTERFACE
SmartGym’s interface now adapts intelligently across different window sizes, orientations, and display shapes. From compact layouts to large and unconventional form factors, the UI automatically makes better use of the available space.

LIQUID GLASS REFINEMENTS
SmartGym’s Liquid Glass design has been expanded across more of the app. Segmented controls, the muscle group picker, custom alerts, and the duration timer have all been refined for a more cohesive and native visual experience.

Grid Diary Classic is now retired

Grid Diary was launched in early 2013 as a paid app. We consistently rolled out free updates, feature upgrades, and customer support for over 6 years.

In January 2019, Grid Diary 2 was released as a brand-new app. We spent over 2 years on new UI design, rewriting every line of code in Swift, building our own sync server… to create the brand-new Grid Diary. Believe it or not, the more we afraid to die out like the small outstanding product (without a steady income to support everlasting development), the more we work hard and value our users.

This app is now renamed to Grid Diary Classic. Users are still able to download it from the App Store. It remains mostly functional, but as software services such as iOS, iCloud, Dropbox change and update, we can no longer keep this legacy app functional.

At this time we recommend transitioning off of Grid Diary Classic into Grid Diary 2 on iOS. Grid Diary 2 was made a free download, and allow users to import their data from Grid Diary Classic at no cost. There is a membership upgrade option via subscription for users that want sync, passcode lock, color themes, and many other new features. We are also offering a 6-month free trial for pro users.

The new subscription model in Grid Diary 2 allows us to continue updating this single version indefinitely. We will never release a new, separate app, all future updates and upgrades will be part of this app binary.

Some of you may be surprised by this change. But it’s the result of a long-term discussion about how to put Grid Diary’s development, and the future of our small team, on a sustainable foundation.

We feel this is best for our users and for the future of Grid Diary. We believe that it will be a life company for you and we want to be around as long as you are to store your memories.

Please visit https://diary-help.sumi.io/migrate-from-classic/ to learn more，feel free to contact me if you have any questions or concerns.

Leave the path and Cyclemeter announces you're off course, reroutes, and lets you know when you're back on. Add your own Custom Cues for the things a map doesn't know: a water stop, a gate, the turn at the red barn.

Saving a Navigation also creates a route, so every workout you record along it is grouped and compared. Routes planned elsewhere work too — a TCX or FIT file from Ride with GPS or cycle.travel keeps its cues when you import it.
